title: Safe execution: unprivileged user, read-only filesystem and capabilities

videos.script: Lesson eight built an image with no shell and a user that is not root. That is a good image. It is not yet a safe container. {{image}} How a container runs is decided by whoever starts it. And the defaults of docker run are generous. A writable filesystem. Fourteen capabilities within reach. No limit on memory. {{defaults}} One flag, user zero, turns linkbox's process into root, and it rewrites its own code. {{root}} So this lesson adds controls that do not care who the process is. You will run linkbox read-only, and watch it fail twice, each time naming the place it needs to write. {{readonly}} Then you take away every capability, and the chance to gain new ones. You will see what the kernel's system-call filter refuses, and what memory and process limits do when a program asks for too much. {{kernel}} Last, the pipeline's staging run starts linkbox exactly that way, and the nightly scan proves nothing broke. {{staging}}
